voice.name: en-GB-SoniaNeural
voice.prosody: Climb a hill before dawn. Soon the sky will fill with hundreds of balloons. It is still dark and cold. From the valleys below comes the roar of burners: the balloons are warming up. Then one lifts off, then dozens, drifting over the fairy chimneys. Wind and rain made these pointed rocks. Long ago, volcanoes threw out ash that hardened into soft stone. Water and wind carved it again and again until these fairy-tale shapes appeared. The rock was so soft that people carved it too: homes, dovecotes, storerooms, churches. For centuries monks lived in these valleys and painted their prayers inside the stone. At the Göreme Open Air Museum, duck through a church doorway. As your eyes adjust, colours appear on the walls. Little light gets into the Dark Church, so its frescoes still look fresh. When the day brightens, walk down into a valley. Among the rocks you will find a window, a stair, a room. Put your hand on the stone: nature shaped this place, and people made it home.
